response: Increasing the sample size causes the sampling distribution of the sample mean to become more normally distributed (if not already), reduces its spread (standard deviation decreases by a factor of $\sqrt{n}$), and makes the graph steeper and thinner. It also narrows confidence intervals by decreasing the error bound.

To flag unusually low or high observations (outliers), calculate the Interquartile Range (IQR) by subtracting the first quartile ($Q_1$) from the third quartile ($Q_3$). Observations below $Q_1 - 1.5 \times IQR$ are flagged as unusually low, and those above $Q_3 + 1.5 \times IQR$ are flagged as unusually high.

The ordinary mean is skewed by outliers because it uses all values; a trimmed mean removes extreme observations from both ends to provide a more representative center; and the median, which focuses on the middle value of an ordered dataset, is not affected at all by the numerical values of outliers.
